decks.module: Blood alcohol and the DWI offense
decks.domain: Alcohol, impaired driving and the law

cards.front: At what blood alcohol concentration is every driver impaired?
cards.back: At a blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, of zero point zero eight percent every driver is impaired, and many people are affected at far lower levels.

cards.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does crash risk begin to rise?
cards.back: Crash risk begins rising at a BAC of zero point zero five percent, and at zero point zero eight percent the chance of causing a fatal crash is greater still.
cards.memory_hook: risk rises at point oh five

cards.front: Is a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five the legal limit for a car driver?
cards.back: The zero point zero five figure is where crash risk starts to rise, not a legal limit; the legal per se limit for a car driver is zero point zero eight.
cards.memory_hook: five is risk, eight is law

cards.front: What did the Safe Roads Act do to North Carolina drunk-driving laws?
cards.back: The Safe Roads Act of nineteen eighty-three replaced all earlier North Carolina drunk-driving laws with a single offense called Driving While Impaired, or DWI.

cards.front: How can DWI be proven without any blood alcohol number?
cards.back: DWI can be proven by showing that alcohol, drugs or both appreciably impaired the driver's physical or mental faculties.

cards.front: Which blood alcohol levels prove DWI for a car driver and for a commercial driver?
cards.back: DWI can also be proven by a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or more, or zero point zero four or more when driving a commercial motor vehicle.

cards.front: How does the per se DWI limit for a commercial vehicle driver compare with an ordinary driver's?
cards.back: The per se DWI limit is zero point zero eight for an ordinary driver but zero point zero four for a driver of a commercial motor vehicle.

cards.front: What checks may law enforcement set up under the DWI laws?
cards.back: North Carolina DWI laws allow law enforcement to set up roadblocks to check for impaired drivers.

decks.domain: Alcohol, impaired driving and the law

cards.front: What will a driver charged with DWI be asked to do?
cards.back: A driver charged with DWI will be asked to take a chemical test of breath or blood.

cards.front: What happens to your license if you refuse a required chemical test?
cards.back: Refusing a required chemical test brings an immediate license revocation of at least thirty days and a further DMV revocation of at least twelve months.

cards.front: After a willful-refusal revocation, when might a judge grant a limited driving privilege?
cards.back: In some cases, once six months of a willful-refusal revocation have passed, a judge may grant a limited driving privilege.

cards.front: What happens right away if your chemical test result is at or over the limit?
cards.back: A test result of zero point zero eight or more, or zero point zero four or more in a commercial motor vehicle, means your driving privilege is revoked immediately for at least thirty days.
cards.memory_hook: fail the test, lose it now

cards.front: How do the penalties for refusing the chemical test compare with failing it?
cards.back: Refusing the chemical test brings at least thirty days of immediate revocation plus at least twelve months from DMV, while failing it at zero point zero eight or more brings an immediate revocation of at least thirty days.

cards.front: Can a test result or a refusal be used against you in court?
cards.back: Both your chemical test result and any refusal to be tested can be used as evidence in court.

decks.domain: Alcohol, impaired driving and the law

cards.front: May you drink a beer while driving?
cards.back: Drinking any alcoholic beverage while driving, beer included, is prohibited.

cards.front: May you carry an open container of alcohol in a car's passenger area?
cards.back: Carrying an open container of any alcoholic beverage in a vehicle, including in the passenger area, is prohibited.

cards.front: What alcohol is allowed in the passenger area of a commercial vehicle on a public road?
cards.back: In the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on a public road, alcohol is banned whether the container is open or closed.

cards.front: How does the container rule for a car differ from the rule for a commercial vehicle?
cards.back: An open container is banned anywhere in a car's passenger area, while in a commercial vehicle's passenger area even closed containers are banned.
cards.memory_hook: cars ban open, trucks ban all

decks.domain: Alcohol, impaired driving and the law

cards.front: How do DWI punishment levels work, and what does a second conviction require?
cards.back: Punishment levels rise with the seriousness of the offense, and a second DWI conviction requires time in jail.

cards.front: Besides punishment, what do DWI laws aim to do for offenders?
cards.back: DWI laws aim to help offenders with alcohol problems as well as punish them: repeat offenders and high-BAC drivers are checked for an alcohol problem, and lower-BAC offenders attend alcohol safety school.

cards.front: What must anyone convicted of DWI complete before driving privileges return?
cards.back: Anyone convicted of DWI must complete a substance abuse assessment before driving privileges are reinstated.

cards.front: What license revocation does a first DWI conviction bring?
cards.back: A first DWI conviction brings a mandatory one-year license revocation.

cards.front: When does a second DWI conviction bring a four-year revocation?
cards.back: A second DWI conviction brings a mandatory four-year revocation when the earlier offense happened within three years of the current one.

cards.front: When does a third DWI conviction bring permanent revocation?
cards.back: A third DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent revocation if at least one earlier conviction happened within the past five years.

cards.front: What does a fourth DWI conviction bring, and when is it a felony?
cards.back: A fourth DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent revocation, and it is a felony if the three earlier convictions all happened within the past seven years.

cards.front: Which look-back windows apply to the second, third and fourth DWI convictions?
cards.back: Look-back windows differ by conviction: three years for the four-year second-offense revocation, five years for permanent revocation on a third, seven years for the felony fourth.

decks.domain: Alcohol, impaired driving and the law

cards.front: When is a blood alcohol concentration restriction placed on a license?
cards.back: A blood alcohol concentration restriction is placed on a license restored after a DWI suspension, or on a Limited Driving Privilege granted after a DWI conviction.

cards.front: What is the BAC restriction on a first restoration, and on later ones?
cards.back: The restriction is zero point zero four on the first restoration and zero point zero zero on the second or any later restoration.

cards.front: How does the restored-license BAC restriction change after the first restoration?
cards.back: The restored-license BAC restriction is zero point zero four the first time and zero point zero zero for every later restoration.

cards.front: Which convictions bring a zero-level BAC restriction from the start?
cards.back: The restriction is also zero point zero zero after a DWI conviction in a commercial motor vehicle, a conviction for driving under twenty-one after consuming alcohol or drugs, or felony death by vehicle.

cards.front: Which DWI convictions require an ignition interlock device?
cards.back: A DWI conviction with a BAC of zero point one five or more, or with another conviction in the past seven years, requires an ignition interlock device on the vehicle.

cards.front: How does the ignition interlock trigger differ from the fourth-offense felony rule?
cards.back: The ignition interlock is triggered by a BAC of zero point one five or more or a prior conviction within seven years, while a fourth conviction becomes a felony when three priors fall within seven years.

cards.front: What may the court do if you are convicted of DWI while revoked for an earlier DWI?
cards.back: If you are convicted of DWI while already revoked for an earlier DWI, the court may order your vehicle seized and sold.

decks.domain: Alcohol, impaired driving and the law

cards.front: What is the legal age to buy alcohol in North Carolina?
cards.back: The legal age to buy any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is twenty-one, and anyone younger who buys or tries to buy alcohol breaks the law.

cards.front: What penalty does an underage person face for buying or trying to buy alcohol?
cards.back: An underage person convicted of buying or trying to buy alcohol, or of helping another underage person do so, faces a one-year license revocation.

cards.front: What happens to an underage person who uses a fake or borrowed ID to get alcohol?
cards.back: An underage person convicted of using, or trying to use, a fake license or ID or someone else's license or ID to get alcohol faces a one-year revocation.

cards.front: What penalty faces someone who lends an ID to an underage buyer or gives alcohol to an underage person?
cards.back: Any person convicted of letting an underage person use their license or ID to buy alcohol, or of giving alcohol to an underage person, also faces a one-year revocation.

cards.front: Does an adult who helps an underage person get alcohol face a lighter penalty than the buyer?
cards.back: An adult who lends an ID to an underage buyer or gives alcohol to an underage person faces the same one-year revocation as the underage buyer.

cards.front: What happens to a driver under twenty-one convicted of driving with any alcohol or drugs in their body?
cards.back: A driver under twenty-one convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body loses their license for one year.

cards.front: How does the alcohol standard for drivers under twenty-one differ from the adult standard?
cards.back: Drivers under twenty-one face an any-amount rule for alcohol or drugs with a one-year revocation, unlike adults, who are measured against the per se BAC limit.

recaps.module: Blood alcohol and the DWI offense

recap_hooks.text: Risk rises at point oh five; the legal limit is point oh eight.
Commercial drivers are held to point oh four.
Refuse the test and lose your license longer, with a year added from DMV.
Fail the test and lose your license right away for at least thirty days.
No drinking while driving and no open containers in a car.
In a commercial vehicle's passenger area, no alcohol at all, open or closed.
First DWI means one year without a license.
Look back three, five and seven years for the second, third and fourth.
After DWI, the first restoration allows point oh four, then zero.
A high BAC or a recent prior means an ignition interlock.
Twenty-one to buy, and buying, fake IDs or helping cost a year.
Under twenty-one, any alcohol or drugs while driving costs a year.
